files.reason: Collision-level STATS19 records for 2024 (exact URL observed on the gov.uk Road Safety Data release page). ~18.6 MB, exceeds WebFetch's 10 MB read limit so contents were not summarized in-tool, but the sibling casualty CSV of the same release downloaded and parsed as valid CSV with a 24-column header; this collision table supplies the primary record table with collision_index and observed values/identifiers. Independent download/parse required to confirm header and row count.

Vehicle-level STATS19 records for 2024 (exact URL observed on the same gov.uk release page). ~20.3 MB, exceeds in-tool read limit, so format confirmed only by the verified sibling table; supplies vehicle-level records joinable via collision_index + vehicle_reference. Needs independent download to confirm.

Casualty-level records for 2024; verified directly. Header observed: collision_index, collision_year, collision_ref_no, vehicle_reference, casualty_reference, casualty_class, sex_of_casualty, age_of_casualty, age_band_of_casualty, casualty_severity, pedestrian_location, pedestrian_movement, car_passenger, bus_or_coach_passenger, pedestrian_road_maintenance_worker, casualty_type, casualty_imd_decile, lsoa_of_casualty, enhanced_casualty_severity, casualty_injury_based, casualty_adjusted_severity_serious, casualty_adjusted_severity_slight, casualty_distance_banding, escooter_flag. Provides observed values and record-level identifiers for validation.

Official DfT Road Safety Open Dataset Data Guide 2025 (native XLSX, 83.1 KB, downloaded successfully; ZIP/OOXML structure with >=2 worksheets confirmed). This is the field-definitions and value-label document accompanying the 2024 CSVs, giving variable names, codes/units and collection notes needed to interpret records. Sheet text not legible via WebFetch binary; requires independent parse.

DfT severity-adjustment figure guidance (native DOCX, downloaded; valid OOXML container confirmed). Documents the methodology DfT applies to correct reported-injury-severity misclassification — a directly applicable statistical/quality criterion for judging fitness of casualty_severity fields. Text not legible via WebFetch binary; requires independent extraction.

STATS19 review final report (native PDF, valid %PDF-1.6, 2.2 MB, downloaded). Independently published review enumerating coverage, under-reporting and quality limitations of the STATS19 collection — an authoritative reference for quality criteria and known-invalidity considerations. Text is Flate-compressed; requires independent extraction.

cases.identity: DfT STATS19 Road Safety Open Data (Great Britain reported road casualties) — linked collision / vehicle / casualty tables with companion data guide and severity-adjustment methodology, for 2024 data year, published September 2025 by the UK Department for Transport on gov.uk
missing_information: No native (non-HTML) consolidated background quality report: the DfT 'Reported road casualty statistics: background quality report' and 'Known data issues' pages exist only as HTML on gov.uk, so i4 is anchored on the severity-adjustment DOCX and the STATS19 review PDF instead of a single native quality statement.

2024 collision and vehicle CSVs (~19-20 MB) exceeded WebFetch's read limit, so their headers/row counts were not confirmed in-tool; only the casualty CSV was directly parsed. Independent download is required to confirm all three headers and that the 2024 year is complete.

The 2024 data guide variables, units and value codes could not be read in-tool (binary XLSX); the mapping of guide fields to the observed CSV headers and the specific statistical-testing conventions used by DfT remain to be confirmed on extraction.

rejected_candidates.reason: US BTS airline on-time dataset is a JavaScript/form-based field-selection interface with no directly downloadable native file URL observed, so no stable native artifact could be captured; dropped in favor of a case with directly downloadable native CSVs plus a codebook.

Truncated/opaque URL that returned HTTP 500 (and earlier a generic redirect); it is not an observed complete attachment path and content could not be established, so it was not treatable as a native i3 document.
This data.dft.gov.uk copy returned HTTP 404; the working severity-adjustment DOCX is only the assets.publishing.service.gov.uk copy, which was retained instead.
Generic repository landing pages returned by broad queries; blocked by JavaScript verification and contained no identifiable case-bearing dataset or native artifact.
Generic HDX resource pages surfaced by concatenated keyword queries; no specific dataset, file, or content could be verified against the blueprint nodes, so not a defensible case anchor.

stop_reason: A coherent, real case is defensible: a single DfT collection where raw record tables (i2), a field-definitions data guide (i3) and applicable quality/methodology references (i4) all exist as directly downloadable native files from observed, non-guessed URLs. Two of three 2024 CSVs exceed in-tool read limits and the XLSX/DOCX/PDF require independent extraction, but all URLs are exact observed attachments with verified content types, and file accessibility is distinguished from information coverage. The selected set (3 CSVs + 1 XLSX guide + 1 DOCX + 1 PDF) is within the 6-file materialization limit, uses only retrievable node IDs i2/i3/i4, and leaves only explicitly stated acquisition/verification gaps rather than invented facts.
